text.p: Follwing are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- The two Nobel Peace Prize winners Bishop Carlos Belo and Jose Ramos-Horta held separate news conferences in Oslo on Monday, despite being jointly awarded the honour. Head of the Nobel Committee Francis Sejersted said the committee was following the winners' wishes, but also that the Indonesian embassy had been active.
- People from East Timor, invited to Oslo by the Nobel Committee, are under pressure from Indonesian authorities not to answer any questions that could be seen to be critical of Indonesia.

- Justice Minister Anne Holt has announced that authorities will review applications for residency on humanitarian grounds from refugees with children. The refugees have sought asylum in churches after their first application to stay in Norway was refused.
- Clas Inge Isacson of forestry group Norske Skog ASA says the company expects pulp prices to rise by nine percent in January to $610 per tonne.

- A new book written by Arne Olav Brundtland, the husband of former Norwegian Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland, says the former premier could have been persuaded to become General Secretary of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation a year ago.
